analysis: Examined the benchmark report schema bump to v5 (SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift), the benchmark live-runner environment helper (SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.swift lines 66-81, 101-102), and the new prefill geometry resolution in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. No confidentiality, authentication, attestation or billing surface is touched. The benchmark changes are tooling-only: they record effective prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep and force the simulated geometry via environment keys. The factory change adds env-overridable knobs (DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK, DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS). These are local operator-controlled settings, consistent with the existing trust model where the operator already controls the process environment; they affect performance and memory, not secrecy. Parsing falls back to SDK values on malformed, zero or negative input. The step-budget doubling guards overflow. Gemma 4 gets a wide 2048-token chunk and its media block floor is raised to 1120; this changes memory and activation behavior (availability/DoS, T-029-adjacent) and depends on the paged pool sizing and PagedSequenceKV preconditions, which are outside the supplied evidence. An operator-supplied huge DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK could inflate the paged pool or activation memory, but it is self-inflicted on the operator's own machine and not a cross-boundary regression. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not affected: no KVCacheSSD, cacheSalt or lookup tag code changed. A larger chunk could change block alignment for cache donations, but that code was not supplied. Remaining integration questions: how the paged pool and CBv2MultimodalPlan.validate consume the new geometry, and whether the activation floors (platform-coordinated) remain valid with the new Gemma 4 default. Neither is established as a security issue by the supplied evidence.
